subject: Post-demo: time-to-first-token targets, streaming mode decision and next steps
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lyman <jordan.lyman@edgefin.io>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: time-to-first-token targets, streaming mode decision and next steps

Jordan — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary (what we agreed verbally)
- Target TTFT: median ~150ms for typical 2–3 sentence prompts; P95 <= 300ms.
- Throughput: baseline 200 qps sustained for L1 traffic, with bursts to 800 qps for campaign spikes.
- Concurrency: customer expects support for 1000 concurrent open connections in the region (SSE fanout anticipated).
- Streaming preference: EdgeFin prefers SSE for simplicity and browser compat; WebSocket fallback acceptable for mobile clients.
- Chunk cadence: target server-side chunk emission of ~50–150ms between chunks for a responsive feel; we proposed heartbeat + small chunk priming to avoid perceived stalls.

Open questions / clarifications we need from EdgeFin
1) Typical payload size (tokens per request) and average expected response length (tokens). Helps us select batching/kv-cache tuning.
2) Percentage of requests that require function/tool-calls or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — changes end-to-end latency profile.
3) Any strict TLS/session architecture constraints (long-lived connections behind your proxy) that would affect SSE fanout.

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA)
- Ben (me): share internal TTFT playbook and the demo recording — attached (redwood-ttft-playbook.pdf, redwood-demo-recording.mp4). Action: today EOD.
- Karthik: prepare a probing harness that reproduces your sample payloads and measures median/P95 TTFT across sequence lengths. Action: probe draft by Thu 7/22.
- Jordan: send 3 representative payloads (short/medium/long) and confirm whether tool-calls/RAG will be in-scope for pilot. Action: reply to this thread.
- Rishi: scope pilot configuration (concurrency, autoscale triggers, fallback policy) and prepare a short SLO proposal for your review. Action: initial SLO doc by Fri 7/23.

Notes on fallback behavior / graceful degradation
- If SSE fanout becomes constrained we will route new traffic to a WebSocket-backed path with slightly higher latency but preserved ordering.
- We will enable prefix + KV caching for repeated prompts to reduce per-token execution where applicable.

Attachment stubs: redwood-ttft-playbook.pdf (internal playbook with measurement methodology), redwood-demo-recording.mp4 (demo video).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m follow-up if helpful.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: time-to-first-token targets, streaming mode decision and next steps

Thanks Ben — really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
- The average prompt we expect to send is ~75 tokens (short) with 20% long-form at ~400 tokens. Responses average ~120 tokens.
- We will definitely use RAG for about 30% of requests (internal docs + pricing tables).
- Our infra team prefers SSE for desktop but will want a WebSocket fallback for older mobile clients.

I attached a link to a sample payloads JSON (I'll paste it below) and flagged the RAG cases. Can you confirm whether your measurement harness will include simulated RAG latency (i.e., extra DB lookup 50–100ms) or if we should strip that out for the TTFT baseline?

Sample payloads (inline):
- short.json (prompt ~60 tokens)
- medium.json (prompt ~180 tokens)
- long.json (prompt ~420 tokens)

Jordan Lyman

jordan.lyman@edgefin.io

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lyman <jordan.lyman@edgefin.io>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: time-to-first-token targets, streaming mode decision and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the sample sizes, that helps a lot. Quick technical notes on how we will measure TTFT and where RAG fits in: 

Measurement plan (what the harness will do)
- Baseline (no RAG): single-request measured from HTTP request arrival to first token emitted on stream. We'll run 1k samples per payload size and report median, P90, P95.
- RAG probe: we will simulate an external retrieval delay (configurable 0–200ms) to understand end-to-end impact on TTFT. We will publish two numbers: intrinsic TTFT (model-only) and composite TTFT (including retrieval).

Implementation details
- We will enable prefix priming and KV cache for repeated prompts in the probe to mirror production expectations.
- For concurrency shaping we'll test at 200 qps sustained and then step to bursts (400 -> 800 qps) while monitoring queuing latency and backpressure behavior.
- SSE fanout test: we will spin up a small fanout proxy to simulate 1000 concurrent open connections and measure per-connection resource usage.

Pilot ask from EdgeFin
- Can you provide a short-lived API token scoped to a sandbox with representative RAG behavior? If not, send a sample of your retrieval latency distribution and we can run the simulated delays locally.

I attached a minimal spec that would help us configure the harness: edgefin_stream_spec.xlsx (schema: payload examples, expected RAG fraction, preferred chunk cadence).

I will post the initial probe results by Thu 7/22 as noted.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: time-to-first-token targets, streaming mode decision and next steps

Quick update and concrete action items after internal sync: 
- Karthik will run two probes: (A) model-only TTFT (B) composite TTFT w/ 100ms retrieval delay. Deliverable: CSV with median/P95 + per-step load profile. ETA 7/22.
- Rishi will draft an SLO proposal that maps to EdgeFin's target (med 150ms / P95 300ms) and include acceptable error budget / fallback triggers. Deliverable: SLO doc + canary plan ETA 7/23.
- Ben will schedule a 30-minute pilot kickoff for Fri 7/23 @ 11:00am PT — Jordan, can you confirm? I'll share a calendar invite and the HubSpot link here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/0000000/record/EDGE-2027-94

Action table (ready-to-copy)
- Jordan: provide sample payloads + retrieval latency distribution (owner) — due 7/20 (pending)
- Karthik: probe results (owner) — due 7/22
- Rishi: SLO doc + canary plan (owner) — due 7/23
- Ben: pilot kickoff invite + internal access instructions (owner) — done after Jordan confirms

If we get those pieces in place this week we can stand up the pilot next week and aim for a light production-ready SLO by mid-August.

Thanks all — Ben

P.S. Jordan — attaching the internal playbook and the spec Karthik mentioned for convenience.

Attachments referenced: redwood-ttft-playbook.pdf, edgefin_stream_spec.xlsx
